# ImageLabel

- Inherits [`UIObject`](uiobject.md)
- Created with `Instance.new("ImageLabel")`

A UI object that shows an image.

This page lists the members this class declares. Inherited members are
listed on the page of the class that declares them.

## Properties

| Name | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Image` | `Content` | `""` | read/write | The image to show, as an `asset://` path. With an empty value no image is drawn; the background still is. An image that does not exist, or that has not finished loading, is drawn as a plain rectangle of `ImageColor`. |
| `ImageColor` | `Color3` | `Color3.new(1, 1, 1)` | read/write | A color the image is multiplied by, so that one white image can be drawn in any color. White changes nothing. |
| `ImageRectOffset` | `Vector2` | `Vector2.zero` | read/write | The top left corner of the part of the image to show, in pixels of the image. Use it with `ImageRectSize` to show one frame of a sprite sheet or one icon of an atlas. |
| `ImageRectSize` | `Vector2` | `Vector2.zero` | read/write | The size of the part of the image to show, in pixels of the image, starting at `ImageRectOffset`. Zero shows the whole image. A negative size mirrors the image along that axis. |
| `ImageTransparency` | `number` | `0` | read/write | How transparent the image is, from 0 (opaque) to 1 (invisible). It is separate from `BackgroundTransparency`, so an icon can fade while its background stays, or the reverse. A value outside 0 to 1 is kept as set and drawn as the nearer limit. |
| `ScaleType` | `Enum.ScaleType` | `Enum.ScaleType.Stretch` | read/write | How the image fits the object. With `Tile`, an image that would repeat more than about four thousand times is stretched instead. |
| `SliceCenter` | `Rect` | `Rect.new(Vector2.zero, Vector2.zero)` | read/write | For `ScaleType.Slice`: the rectangle that divides the image into nine slices, in pixels of the image. The four corners are drawn at their own size whatever the size of the object, so a panel keeps its rounded corners.<br><br>If the object is narrower than the two corners together, the center is removed and the corners do not overlap. An empty or inverted rectangle is used as given. |
